writeup: TIC 152676628 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 1.01% occurring every 5.2599 days, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal achieved a detection significance of 159.1 using the Box Least Squares algorithm, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 20.7, though the centroid offset of 5.4 arcseconds warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel target. The machine-learning screening score of 0.83 suggests the pipeline's model assesses this as likely to be a genuine target star, and the candidate passed all data quality checks.
